title: Who's Who: Henri Duval
summary: Aperture critic whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Henri Duval (born 1836) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a aperture critic whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Duval is the most influential living critic within Eidetics, known for finding ordinary diffraction, flawed clocks, and suggestive labeling behind purported miracles. He accepts controlled apertures but rejects claims that the Stratum possesses intention.
His public debates are crowded because he has withdrawn several of his own celebrated conclusions.

For Alderwick readers, Henri Duval stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
